label: Reaper patchwork along every populated descent
definition: ReaperPatchwork R h Concrete w holds when, in every history v accessible from w, along every strictly descending sequence of moments c whose first moment is populated by a contingent concrete individual in v: if every two adjacent local pieces are realized together in some world accessible from v, then some single world accessible from v realizes every piece along c. In ordinary language: possible, pairwise co-possible Reaper pieces placed at the moments of a descent can be glued into one possible arrangement.
note: Analyst countable gluing premise in the style of Koons's infinitary spatiotemporal and causal-network patchwork (PInfSP, CPNPP; docs/notes/causal-finitism-367.md); attribution deferred. Because no world realizes every piece along a descent (GrimReaperPatchwork arrangementImpossible, a theorem), this typed premise for a given frame is equivalent to 'along every populated descent, adjacent pieces are not all co-possible', and founded populated pasts are equivalent to it together with ReaperPiecesPossible for the same frame. Control 1 (patchwork holding in a beginningless history) holds only because its antecedent fails there. The split into two premises is informative only through their separate motivations: the warrant for patchwork must come from the general recombination principle it instantiates, not from this instance. A general gluing principle over arbitrary world properties is false for trivial reasons, so that principle must be restricted to suitable pieces; note that a piece is not purely local (its admissibility clause refers to the whole descent). Ranging over every descent, together with local pieces it also excludes contingent presence after the first moment of a dense past. OPEN.
